Same-location conflict uses combat or opposed vehicle control within chase action economy
Cut to the chase establishes the opening range and location chain
A quarry may escape by breaking contact or hiding when the pursuer cannot relocate it
CON or Drive Auto speed rolls adjust MOV for the chase and determine participation
Hazards allow cautious bonus dice; failure still advances and costs damage plus 1D3 movement actions
Joining participants and changed movement modes recalculate speed/action state as specified
Each participant has one action plus one per MOV above the slowest participant
Multiple-character chases eliminate outpaced participants and position each side by MOV
Pushed rolls are not used during an active chase
Passengers act once; moving fire takes a penalty die while stopped fire costs one movement action
Pedal to the Metal trades one action for 2-5 locations with penalty dice
Chase rounds act in DEX order; tied DEX uses an opposed DEX roll
The lead quarry may choose alternate routes
Players and Keeper alternate Luck calls for sudden Regular hazards
Vehicle MOV, Build, armor, passengers, impairment, and collision severity come from Tables V and VI
Ordinary physical armor subtracts its rating from incoming damage
Automatic fire resolves declared ammunition in volleys with recoil penalties and per-volley hits
Combat rolls cannot be pushed
Combatants act from highest DEX to lowest with combat skill breaking ties
Melee dodge is opposed and ties favor the dodging defender
A combatant may flee close combat on their action if an escape route is open and they are unrestrained
Extreme attacks maximize damage and penetrating weapons add an impale damage roll
Melee fight back is opposed and ties favor the initiating attacker
Cover, diving, point blank, aiming, speed, size, reloading, and multiple shots modify firearm attacks
Base, long, and very-long range set Regular, Hard, and Extreme difficulty
Firearm attacks are normally unopposed and failure deals no damage
An attack roll at or above a weapon malfunction rating jams or misfires the weapon
Fighting maneuvers use Build penalties and become impossible at a three-point deficit
A successful fighting maneuver applies its declared non-damage goal
After a target defends in a round subsequent melee attackers gain a bonus die
Ranged and thrown attacks use firearm range difficulty and limited close defense
A readied firearm acts at DEX plus fifty
Combat proceeds in elastic rounds with one action opportunity per capable character
Weapon special effects include bounded Stun and escalating Burn
An unanticipated surprise attack may hit automatically or gain a bonus die
Successful attacks apply weapon damage and unarmed attacks use 1D3
Weapon profiles define skill, damage, range, uses, capacity, malfunction, and era
Bonus and penalty dice cancel one-for-one then extra tens dice
Semantic skill, characteristic, and opponent references select the check; numeric targets are host-locked from the canonical investigator sheet or authored opponent state before resolver execution
A combined skill roll uses one investigator's single D100 result against every named skill; the Keeper declares whether any or all named skills must succeed
Regular / Hard (half) / Extreme (fifth) required success levels
Roll only for an uncertain consequential outcome; the player's intention defines one clear goal and the Keeper selects the fitting skill or characteristic
Multiple investigators use separate rolls or a situation-specific cooperation procedure; a repeated attempt at the same goal generally becomes a pushed roll
Non-combat opposed rolls use one roll per side, compare success levels, break a tied successful level by higher skill or characteristic, and cannot be pushed
1D100 succeeds when the roll is less than or equal to the effective target

An Extreme check cannot overcome opposition more than 100 plus the investigator's skill or characteristic; multiple investigators may reduce the opposing characteristic through the stated sequential procedure
Critical is a natural 1; fumble is 96-100 below 50% target else 100
Each development phase reduces per-creature habituation totals by one
Roll 1D100; above current skill or above 95 gains 1D10 and may exceed 100
After each session, D100 above current Luck gains 1D10, capped at 99
A roll altered by Luck earns no skill improvement check
A skill attaining 90 or more during development grants 2D6 current SAN
Each checked skill receives at most one improvement roll per development phase
Development may include self-help, finance review, backstory changes, and awfulness-limit decay
Development occurs at a scenario/chapter end or a suitable narrative pause
A successful skill use earns one check; bonus-die-only successes and opposed losers do not
Cthulhu Mythos and Credit Rating never receive improvement checks

Unstabilized dying: CON at the end of the next round and every round, failure is death; only First Aid can stabilize. Stabilized dying: CON each hour; failure loses the temporary HP and reverts to the round clock
0 HP plus Major Wound ticked is dying: record HP 0 and check the dying box

First Aid within one hour grants 1 HP; may be attempted once, later attempts are Pushed; two people may work together (either success); on a dying patient it only temporarily stabilizes (+1 temporary HP, followed by Medicine)
A single attack dealing more than maximum HP kills outright
The Major Wound marker is erased by an Extreme recovery roll, or any time current HP has recovered to half or more of maximum HP
On a Major Wound: tick the box, fall prone, make a CON roll to stay conscious; 0 HP while ticked means dying
A single attack dealing half or more of maximum HP is a Major Wound (rounded up)

computed_threshold.source_example: 15 hit points, damage of 8 or more is a major wound

nodes.name: Medicine takes at least one hour, works any time after damage, and raises difficulty to Hard when not performed the same day; success restores 1D3 in addition to First Aid; a dying character needs successful First Aid before Medicine can stabilize
Without a Major Wound ticked, recover 1 HP per day

While the Major Wound box is ticked, make a CON recovery roll at the end of each week: fail = no recovery, success = 1D3, Extreme = 2D3 and erase the marker; bonus die for complete rest in a comfortable environment; bonus die for effective medical care (caregiver Medicine roll first); penalty die for poor environment/insufficient rest or a caregiver Medicine fumble; a fumble creates a lasting injury/complication
No negative HP; 0 HP is unconscious; further damage ignored but a sincere kill attempt succeeds; regular damage cannot kill at 0 HP
A significantly disrupted casting fails but still pays SAN and MP costs
A newly learned spell requires a Hard POW roll; later casts and NPC casts need no casting roll
Chapter 12 defines spell costs, casting times, effects, variations, and deeper versions
Book study typically takes 2D6 weeks and uses a Hard INT roll unless success is automatic
Entity teaching may require an INT roll and suggests at least 1D6 SAN loss
Personal teaching uses the book rules but typically takes 1D8 days
MP equals POW/5, overspends damage HP one-for-one, and regenerates by POW tier
A failed pushed casting still works and costs the spell cost multiplied by 1D6 with dire side effects
Psychology has a base chance of ten percent
The Keeper may roll Psychology concealed and announce only gained information
Psychology can oppose Disguise
After failure information may be true or false and its reliability stays unknown
Opposing social skill below 50 is Regular and 50 through 89 is Hard
Psychology opposes Charm, Fast Talk, Intimidate, and Persuade
Psychology studies a person to infer motives and character
A successful Psychology roll reveals the truth
Push and Luck decisions hydrate the original canonical persisted roll receipt and a machine-issued continuation grant; caller-supplied or ephemeral receipt identity cannot authorize execution
Keeper states the failure consequence and the player changes approach before the push is confirmed
Only a failed skill or characteristic roll may be pushed; Luck, Sanity, combat, damage, and Sanity-loss amount rolls may not be pushed
A push changes the method and consumes time; the goal must remain achievable, and the skill and difficulty normally remain unchanged unless the situation changes
After a session, roll D100: above current Luck gains 1D10 Luck, otherwise none; Luck caps at 99 and never resets to its starting value
A Luck roll is a percentile check against current Luck; a group uses the lowest individual Luck roll
Spend Luck 1-for-1 after a skill/characteristic roll to lower the total toward the target

Luck spend is limited to the investigator's own skill or characteristic roll and current Luck; it cannot alter Luck, damage, SAN, SAN-loss, or pushed rolls, nor remove criticals, fumbles, firearm malfunctions, or earn an improvement check
A pushed roll is one reroll only after a failed non-pushed check
A real-time bout lasts 1D10 combat rounds under Keeper control
An isolated or group-wide bout may be summarized over 1D10 hours and can be interrupted
A failed SAN roll causes a Keeper-chosen momentary involuntary action
A fumbled SAN roll loses the encounter maximum
Repeated exposure can cap SAN loss from one Mythos creature type
Losing one fifth of current SAN in one Keeper-defined day triggers indefinite insanity
Indefinite treatment is checked monthly or resolves at the Keeper's chapter boundary
Maximum Sanity is 99 minus current Cthulhu Mythos skill
Mythos-induced insanity grants Cthulhu Mythos skill and lowers maximum SAN
Optional insane insight may reveal a useful clue or action
Optional simultaneous-monster handling may use one roll and the highest loss
Optional Mythos hardening changes future Mythos SAN loss and personality
SAN zero causes permanent insanity and ends player control
Phobia and mania exposure impose their stated penalties while insane
A reality check can dispel delusion; failure loses one SAN and starts a bout
A SAN roll compares 1D100 with current Sanity and selects success or failure loss
Keeper awards, skill mastery, monthly psychotherapy, and self-help can raise current SAN within maximum
Temporary insanity ends after 1D10 hours or safe sleep
Five or more SAN from one source prompts INT; success triggers temporary insanity
Any further SAN loss during underlying insanity starts another bout
Player describes conduct; the Keeper then chooses Charm, Fast Talk, Intimidate, or Persuade
A non-neutral motive adjustment is grounded by host-resolved authored NPC agenda, fact, or state evidence bound to the exact target and goal; free prose cannot supply motive evidence
Charm uses warmth, attraction, flattery, or seduction and cannot compel behavior completely contrary to the target's normal behavior
Extreme is the lowest rollable chance; rare circumstances may make the present goal impossible and allow no roll
Fast Talk is quick deception or misdirection; its effect is temporary, though a higher success may last longer
Roleplay first and roll only for a genuine possible conflict; story position, approach, and the NPC's weakness determine whether the goal is automatic, rollable, or presently impossible
Intimidate uses force, threats, or psychological pressure; a credible powerful threat may support the case and a pushed failure may carry out the threat
Positive inclination grants agreement without a roll; neutrality leaves difficulty unchanged; strong opposition raises one or two levels; a substantive supporting case lowers one level
Base difficulty uses the higher of the matching interpersonal skill or Psychology: below 50 Regular, 50-89 Hard, 90+ Extreme

A successful social skill never compels another player's investigator; refusal lets the coercer hold one penalty die for one later roll of the coercer's choice, not indefinitely and never stacking per pair
Persuade uses reasoned argument and normally takes at least half an hour; depending on the goal and time invested its effect may persist
The player's intention defines the goal of the social attempt
